findings.title: Multiple Critical and High Severity Vulnerabilities Detected in Web Server
findings.description: The Nmap vulnerability scan identified numerous known vulnerabilities with associated exploits, including CVE-2019-10098 (HTTP/2 Rapid Reset), CVE-2023-45802 (Log4Shell variant or similar high-severity issues), and multiple others ranging from severity 6.1 to 7.5. These vulnerabilities allow remote code execution, denial of service, and other critical attacks without requiring authentication.

findings.title: Drupal Information Disclosure and Potential Authentication Bypass
findings.description: The NMAP scan reveals a web server running Apache httpd version 2.4.25 with Drupal installed. The output explicitly discloses the exact software versions (Apache/2.4.25, Drupal) via HTTP headers and banners, which aids attackers in targeting known vulnerabilities for these specific versions. Furthermore, multiple sensitive administrative paths are exposed without authentication barriers: /admin/, /user/login/, /user/register/, /node/add/, and specifically /core/install.php. The presence of 'Requested resource was /core/install.php' indicates that the Drupal installation is incomplete or misconfigured (default install page accessible), which often allows attackers to bypass login requirements, execute arbitrary code via SQL injection during setup, or access default credentials.
